summary.text: On January 25, 2024, the FTC announced 6(b) orders to five companies seeking information about investments and partnerships involving generative AI companies and major cloud service providers. The FTC has described using existing legal authorities and Section 5 to address deceptive or unfair AI-related practices, including AI claims and schemes. In 2026, the FTC proposed a policy statement on applying Section 5’s deceptive-practices prohibition to companies marketing AI systems, including concerns about steering AI outputs away from user expectations. The FTC also said it intends to study how companies offering AI companions monetize user engagement and protect children online.

statements.text: Notably, there is no AI exemption from the laws on the books. Accordingly, the FTC will vigorously use the full range of its authorities to protect Americans from deceptive and unfair conduct and maintain open, fair, and competitive markets.

statements.text: The FTC submits this comment to: (1) explain its interest and expertise in promoting fair competition and protecting Americans from unfair or deceptive practices in an economy in which AI is being rapidly deployed; (2) identify several issues raised by generative AI that implicate competition and consumer protection policy, as well as copyright policy; and (3) augment the record in this proceeding with a brief summary and full transcript of an October 4, 2023 FTC roundtable at which creative professionals described the effects of generative AI on their work.

statements.text: The FTC has a long history of cracking down on deceptive advertising and marketing practices, and we will not hesitate to enforce the rules of the road in the context of AI applications.
